meta.title: Who really said "Solitude is independence"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: The sentence appears in Hermann Hesse’s Steppenwolf, in Basil Creighton’s 1929 English translation, page 48. It belongs to Harry Haller’s fictional reflections.

author.heading: About Hermann Hesse
author.bio: Hermann Hesse wrote Demian, Siddhartha and Steppenwolf, novels concerned with identity, inner conflict and spiritual development. Born in Germany, he became a Swiss citizen and received the 1946 Nobel Prize in Literature.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Harry Haller has achieved the solitude he wanted, but the passage also registers his longing for human warmth. The sentence is therefore part of an uneasy account of freedom and loneliness, rather than an uncomplicated instruction to avoid other people.
